description_nl: De bestuurlijke indeling van Nederland in gemeenten, provincies en het landsgebied. Jaarlijks bijgewerkt per 1 januari met eventuele gemeentelijke herindelingen.
description_en: The administrative division of the Netherlands into municipalities (gemeenten), provinces (provincies), and national territory (landgebied). Updated annually on January 1st to reflect any municipal mergers.

provider.name: Kadaster
provider.name_en: Netherlands Cadastre, Land Registry and Mapping Agency

context.administrative_structure: The Netherlands has a three-tier administrative structure: Rijk (national) -> 12 Provincies (provinces) -> 342 Gemeenten (municipalities, as of 2026). Each layer nests within the one above. The gemeentegebied layer includes fields that link each municipality to its parent province.
context.merger_history: The number of Dutch municipalities has been declining for decades through mergers (herindelingen). Recent counts: 2020: 355, 2021: 352, 2022: 345, 2023: 342, 2024: 342, 2025: 342, 2026: 342. Mergers always take effect on January 1st.
context.code_system: CBS (Statistics Netherlands) assigns municipality codes. These are stable numeric codes (4 digits) that do not change. When municipalities merge, the new municipality gets a new code. The 'code' field in this dataset adds a prefix: GM for gemeenten, PV for provincies. These coded identifiers are used across all Dutch government datasets, making this dataset the fundamental reference for spatial joins.
context.relationship_to_cbs: CBS publishes a broader dataset called 'Gebiedsindelingen' (area classifications) which includes many more boundary types: COROP regions, labor market regions (arbeidsmarktregio), safety regions (veiligheidsregio), water boards (waterschappen), and more. The Bestuurlijke Gebieden from Kadaster is the authoritative source for the three core administrative levels.

notes: This dataset covers European Netherlands only (not the Caribbean municipalities Bonaire, Sint Eustatius, Saba).
The GeoPackage contains all three layers in a single file.
CRS is EPSG:28992 (Amersfoort / RD New), the standard Dutch national coordinate system.
For import into the Portolan catalog, each layer should be converted to a separate GeoParquet file and reprojected to EPSG:4326 (WGS84).
